title: A missing underscore sent innocent man to prison for 18 months
titleZh: 一个下划线缺失导致无辜者入狱18个月
author: quantified
relevanceReason: 命中 2 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: One missing underscore in a Skyrim-themed username put an innocent Nova Scotia man in prison for 18 months. A 2018 child-luring investigation, which began in Madison, Wisconsin, and eventually extended to Halifax, Canada, was based on a false premise. Police were looking for a man using the Kik messaging service under the name “fus__ro_dah” (two underscores after “fus”), but they accidentally requested records for the username “fus_ro_dah” (one underscore after “fus”). This one-character difference led them not to the perpetrator but to a Canadian man named Brandon Klayme. (Ars readers may recognize “fus ro dah” as the Unrelenting Force “dragon shout” from The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim.) Despite finding no evidence of the crime on his digital devices, Canadian police arrested Klayme in 2020 on child sex abuse charges. He was convicted after a trial in 2023 and sentenced in 2024 to 18 months in prison. He served the full term. Even after release, Klayme continued to fight his conviction. In the process of preparing his appeal, the username mistake that led to all these years of disruption was finally discovered. On Thursday, the Nova Scotia Court of Appeal overturned Klayme’s conviction, writing: “Mr. Klayme is factually innocent of the offences. He should never have been charged, let alone convicted.” One underscore The case began in 2018. From August through December of that year, a 12-year-old Wisconsin girl communicated with an adult male through the Kik messaging service. During a check of the girl’s phone, her mother found an “inappropriate” photo of the male and called local police. The Dane County Sheriff’s Department responded. A deputy took the phone, and the department ran a forensic search on it. The report identified 125 Kik messages between the girl and an adult with the username “fus__ro_dah” (two underscores after “fus”). To identify this person, the cops contacted Kik, but their subpoena accidentally requested information about the Kik user “fus_ro_dah” (one underscore after “fus”). Kik provided Klayme’s email address in response. Google records showed that this email address was used to access Google services from an IP address in Canada, so the Dane County investigators turned the case over to Halifax Regional Police. Halifax police took the IP address they had been given to local Internet provider Bell Aliant. Bell connected the IP address to the physical address of their subscriber, Brandon Klayme.

comments.author: Aurornis
comments.textRawHtml:
> Nothing linked Klayme to the girl. No intimate images were found. Klayme did have a Kik account, but cops couldn’t even show that he had accessed the service during the period in question.

> Still, Klayme was arrested and hit with three charges:

> Luring a person under 14 years of age by means of telecommunication

> Providing sexually explicit material to a child

> Possession of child pornography

> The case went to trial, where Klayme was found guilty. He then went to prison for 18 months.

What in the world happened in this case?

How can someone be convicted of these charges without any evidence?

Unless the article left something out, the only possible evidence they had was the wrong username. They couldn't even find evidence that this person used Kik at the time of the crime.

What defense did his lawyer even try? I'm so confused.
comments.textZhHtml:
> 没有任何证据将克莱姆与那个女孩联系起来。没有发现亲密照片。 Klayme 确实有一个 Kik 帐户，但警方甚至无法证明他在相关期间访问过该服务。

> 尽管如此，Klayme 仍被捕并被指控三项罪名：

> 通过电信手段引诱 14 岁以下的人

> 向儿童提供露骨色情材料

> 持有儿童色情制品

> 该案进入审判阶段，Klayme 被判有罪。然后他入狱了 18 个月。

这起案件到底发生了什么？

在没有任何证据的情况下，怎么能被定罪？

除非文章遗漏了什么，否则他们唯一可能的证据就是错误的用户名。他们甚至找不到此人在犯罪时使用 Kik 的证据。

他的律师甚至尝试过什么辩护？我很困惑。

children.author: shusaku
children.textRawHtml: It all comes down to the jury, none of those things matter. The bigger issue here: he knew those messages weren’t him, so the lawyer should’ve gone full force to figure out how this happened. I would guess his lawyer didn’t really believe him
children.textZhHtml: 这一切都取决于陪审团，这些都不重要。这里更大的问题是：他知道这些信息不是他发的，所以律师应该全力以赴弄清楚这是怎么发生的。我猜他的律师并不真正相信他

children.author: thephyber
children.textRawHtml:
It was a judge, not a jury.

And yeah, the trial lawyer failed to make the case, but if the defendant couldn't raise money for a defense, they he likely didn't have any experts to refute the prosecution's evidence.
children.textZhHtml:
这是法官，而不是陪审团。

是的，主审律师未能立案，但如果被告无法筹集辩护资金，他们很可能没有任何专家来反驳检方的证据。

children.author: qingcharles
children.textRawHtml: I don't know about the Canadian justice system, but it's very hard in the USA for defendants to get expert witnesses. The state is supposed to pay, but it's almost never done, and when it is they pay bottom rate for the defendant while having unlimited funds for their own experts.
children.textZhHtml: 我不了解加拿大的司法系统，但在美国，被告很难找到专家证人。国家应该支付费用，但几乎从未这样做过，当支付费用时，他们为被告支付最低费率，同时为自己的专家提供无限的资金。

children.author: OsrsNeedsf2P
children.textRawHtml:
Oh something I can comment on!

A friend of mine was facing a mountain of criminal charges. Photo evidence proved the cops lied. We needed an expert testimony explaining the camera angle and why the photo explained how the cops lied.

I think we called every service qualified for providing such a testimony in Ontario, and a good portion of them across all of Canada. Some were even happy to work with us, until they found out we were testifying against the police. We ended up going international but without luck, and ended up with no expert testimony
children.textZhHtml:
哦，我可以发表评论！

我的一个朋友面临着大量的刑事指控。照片证据证明警察撒了谎。我们需要一份专家证词来解释拍摄角度以及为什么照片解释了警察如何撒谎。

我认为我们称安大略省所有有资格提供此类证词的服务机构，以及加拿大各地的大部分服务机构。有些人甚至很乐意与我们合作，直到他们发现我们在作证指控警方。我们最终走向国际，但运气不佳，最终没有专家证言

children.textRawHtml:

Some were even happy to work with us, until they found out we were testifying against the police. We ended up going international but without luck, and ended up with no expert testimony

This is absolutely horrible to hear!! I know you probably don't want homework, but would you ever consider taking this story to news outlets? I suspect there'd be no compensation, but the uproar might (eventually) result in change.

这绝对是可怕的消息！我知道你可能不想做作业，但你会考虑把这个故事带到新闻媒体吗？我怀疑不会有任何补偿，但骚动可能（最终）导致改变。

children.author: leni536
children.textRawHtml: This is insane. I guess this is because of economic incentives, and expert witnesses risk losing work coming from prosecutors if they ever testify against them?
children.textZhHtml: 这太疯狂了。我想这是因为经济动机，如果专家证人作证反对他们，他们就有可能失去检察官的工作？

children.author: thephyber
children.textRawHtml:
Interesting.

I was actually dismissed from a jury panel partially because I said I don't know if I could trust the experts because my perception is that individual experts either repeatedly testify for only the prosecution or only the defense.
children.textZhHtml:
有趣。

我实际上被陪审团开除，部分原因是我说我不知道我是否可以信任专家，因为我的看法是，个别专家要么反复只为控方作证，要么只为辩方作证。

children.author: e40
children.textRawHtml: You can’t leave is hanging like that!  What happened?
children.textZhHtml:
你不能就这么挂着！ 发生了什么？
奇怪的是，在我的国家，我们有一种文化，科学家们喜欢互相追逐——这就是他们生存的目的！没有什么比破坏他人的声誉更能给你带来名声的了。

推翻信念会让你直接载入史册。人们以重做 90 年代的案件为生，这太荒谬了。

美国有无数的联邦起诉，其内容类似于

1）大量证据表明某人有罪。

2）联邦“专家证人”允许并资助作证指向X人

3）辩护失败

4）如果辩护没有失败，法官会找到辩护专家证人无法提供完整证据的原因论点

5）检方提出认罪协议，否则将被判入狱数亿年

6）当一个人意识到自己的辩护不被允许或不会得到资助时，他们就会放弃，或者接受审判，并因敢于接受审判而被判数亿年。

如果你已经拥有一堆犯罪证据和专家证人，你可以继续堆放，将其扔给某个随机的人并不是一件容易的事，正如我们所见在这里，实际上很简单。

推翻定罪假定被告被错误定罪，并且科学家具有与案件相关的技术技能。

问题在于，这些交叉条件使得相关案件的数量很少，而在普通案件中让专家以低廉的价格为被告作证的要求更高。

如果您不介意的话，那是哪个国家/地区？
我听检察官说过，无罪或有罪并不重要。 重要的是他们能否定罪。
“Clair Obscur：Expedition 33”是一款法国游戏（用户名为 expedition 32），这听起来像是法国人会喜欢的游戏，所以我想到的是法国，但我只是假设。

children.author: mothballed
children.textRawHtml:
There are a gazillion federal prosecutions in the US that go something like

1) Pile of evidence that someone is guilty.

2) Federal "expert witness" allowed and funded to testify it points to X person

3) Defense is broke

4) If defense not broke, judge finds reason why defense expert witness can't present their full argument

5) Prosecution offers plea deal or a gazillion years in jail

6) Person folds when they realize none of their defense is allowed or will be funded, or goes to trial and gets a gazillion years for daring to go to trial.

If you already have a pile of evidence for a crime and an expert witnesses you can keep piling on it's not much of a stretch to dump it on some random person, as we saw here, quite easy actually.

children.author: voakbasda
children.textRawHtml: I have heard prosecutors say that innocent or guilty doesn’t matter.  All that matters is whether they can convict.
children.textZhHtml: 我听检察官说过，无罪或有罪并不重要。  重要的是他们能否定罪。

children.author: qingcharles
children.textRawHtml:
I've known and hung out with a lot of prosecutors. I've never heard one say anything like that outright, but, one of the main issues is that in 99.9% of cases the evidence will not be looked at. They are just not given the time and resources to even take a single glance at the police reports, never mind any forensic evidence. They literally have no idea whether the person is guilty or innocent when they offer a plea deal.

Even your paid defense attorney might never look at the case files at all. Jared from Subway's lawyer got into hot water because he got Jared to take a plea and it turned out he was factually innocent of one of the many offenses he was charged with, and that fact would have been uncovered quickly had the defense attorney ever looked at the evidence, which he said he had not.
children.textZhHtml:
我认识不少检察官，也跟他们打过交道。我从来没听谁这么直白地说过，但是，一个主要问题是，在99.9%的案件中，证据根本不会被审查。他们根本没有时间和资源去哪怕扫一眼警方报告，更别提什么法医证据了。他们在提出认罪协议时，完全不知道当事人是有罪还是无辜。

就连你花钱请的辩护律师可能也根本不看案卷。赛百味贾里德的律师就惹了麻烦，因为他让贾里德认了罪，结果发现贾里德在多项指控中有一项事实上是无辜的，而且如果辩护律师看过证据，这个事实很快就能查清，但他承认自己根本没看过证据。

children.author: thephyber
children.textRawHtml: In the US legal system, the defense isn't given access to the prosecution's evidence used in the case immediately. In fact, lots of plea bargains happen before the defense attorney knows for sure what evidence there is to tie their client to the crime.
children.textZhHtml: 在美国司法体系中，辩护方并不能立即获取控方在案件中使用的证据。事实上，很多认罪协商都是在辩护律师还不确定有哪些证据能将他们的当事人与犯罪联系起来之前就已经达成了。

children.author: qingcharles
children.textRawHtml:
Absolutely. Defense usually has to file a motion, then god forbid the evidence is something like an obscure-format security video; nobody will ever figure out how to get it to the defense or how to play it back.

Most plea bargains are done simply based on the charging instruments.
children.textZhHtml:
完全正确。辩方通常必须提交动议，然后要是证据是某种冷门格式的安全监控视频，那可就麻烦了；根本没人知道怎么把视频交给辩方，也没人知道怎么播放。

大多数认罪协商仅仅是基于控告文书进行的。

children.author: thephyber
children.textRawHtml:
I doubt any professional prosecutors would say this out loud. This is likely a disciplinable or disbarrable statement.

This is effectively a truth, but prosecutors are generally held to high ethical standards, where they are expected to drop cases / not bring cases if the evidence doesn't point specifically to the defendant.

That said, there are occasionally times when prosecutors have been caught hiding / burying / not sharing exculpatory evidence (something the police / prosecution found which would help the defense's case against the prosecution). The only reason to do so would be to sandbag the case against the defendant even when there is a shadow of a doubt in the prosecution's case.
children.textZhHtml:
我怀疑没有任何职业检察官会公开这么说。这很可能是要受纪律处分甚至被吊销执照的言论。

但这实际上是个事实，不过检察官通常被要求遵守较高的职业道德标准，如果证据不能明确指向被告，他们理应撤销案件或不予起诉。

话虽如此，偶尔也会有检察官被发现隐瞒、掩盖或不移交开脱证据（即警方或控方发现的有助于辩方对抗控方的证据）。这么做唯一的目的就是在控方案件尚存疑点时，也要暗中算计被告。

children.author: expedition32
children.textRawHtml:
Weird in my country we have a culture were scientists love going after eachother- its what they live for! Nothing gives you more fame than destroying other people's reputation.

And overturning convictions gets you straight into the history books. It gets so ridiculous that people make their life work out of redoing cases from the 90s.
children.textZhHtml:
奇怪的是，在我的国家，我们有一种文化，科学家们喜欢互相追逐——这就是他们生存的目的！没有什么比破坏他人的声誉更能给你带来名声的了。

推翻信念会让你直接载入史册。人们以重做 90 年代的案件为生，这太荒谬了。

children.author: thephyber
children.textRawHtml:
Overturning convictions presumes that the defendant was wrongfully convicted and that the scientist has the technical skill which is relevant in the case.

The problem is that these intersecting conditions make the number of relevant cases small, while having experts testify for defendants for cheap during mundane cases has MUCH higher demand.

问题在于，这些交叉条件使得相关案件的数量很少，而在普通案件中让专家以低廉的价格为被告作证的要求更高。
